title: MSP-LLM: A Structured Large Language Model Framework for Inorganic Material Synthesis Planning
claim: A two-stage chain predicts intermediate structured outputs first, then conditions the next stage on them to produce the complete result.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right; prompt text panels above module boxes, dashed callouts
description: The figure reads left to right. At far left, a cartoon scientist and a yellow speech box ask which precursor set and synthesis operations to use for a target compound. The main panel has two stage boxes on a lower row. A red Precursor Prediction (PP) box feeds a blue Synthesis Operation Prediction (SOP) box through a red 'Precursor Set' arrow. SOP then feeds a gray Final Output box through a blue 'Synthesis Operations' arrow. A long red return arrow along the bottom carries the precursor set to the final output. Above each stage, tinted panels show example fine-tuning prompts and outputs, with the input prompt above and the output below. Red and blue boxes with dashed connectors label key design elements: decision chain, hierarchical precursor types, and precursor constraint factorization. The gray panel at upper right lists the predicted precursor set and ranked synthesis operation sequences.
caption: Overall framework of MSP-LLM. Given a target material, MSP-LLM first predicts the precursor set (PP), and then, conditioned on the predicted precursors, generates the synthesis operation sequence (SOP), resulting in a MSP. The input–output texts above the PP and SOP LLMs illustrate example prompts used during LLM fine-tuning for each task.
abstract: Material synthesis planning (MSP) remains a fundamental and underexplored bottleneck in AI-driven materials discovery, as it requires not only identifying suitable precursor materials but also designing coherent sequences of synthesis operations to realize a target material. Although several AI-based approaches have been proposed to address isolated subtasks of MSP, a methodology for solving the entire MSP task has yet to be established. We propose MSP-LLM, a structured LLM-based framework that formulates MSP as a two-stage process composed of two constituent subproblems: precursor prediction (PP) and synthesis operation prediction (SOP). Our approach introduces a discrete material class as an intermediate decision variable that organizes both tasks into a chemically consistent decision chain. For SOP, we further incorporate hierarchical precursor types as synthesis-relevant inductive biases and employ precursor constraint factorization that preserves precursor-related information in the autoregressive decoding state. Extensive experiments show that MSP-LLM consistently outperforms existing methods on both PP and SOP, as well as on the MSP task, demonstrating an effective and scalable framework with practical potential for autonomous MSP.
